reason: The order declares a national emergency over the situation in Iran, blocks property of the Government of Iran, its instrumentalities and controlled entities and the Central Bank of Iran within United States jurisdiction, authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to use the powers of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, and states that it is effective immediately and to be transmitted to the Congress and published. Executive Orders 12276 to 12284 and 12294 (January 19 and February 24, 1981) implemented the Algiers Declarations: 12276 to 12281 authorized escrow arrangements or directed the transfer of identified Iranian Government assets once (partial and performed), 12282 revoked the prohibitions in Executive Orders 12205 and 12211 and Proclamation 4702, 12283 barred certain claims, 12284 restricted property of the former Shah's estate and 12294 suspended litigation of claims; none revokes this order. The emergency has been continued by notice every year, most recently on November 5, 2025, and the blocking of property not transferred continues. The one-time sentences on immediate effect, transmittal and publication were carried out at issuance. The clause is operative on 2026-10-14.
